content.title: About
content.content: Sliced ham, restaurant style is a ready‑to‑eat meat product made from selected pork shoulder or loin, cured, smoked and thinly sliced. It has a tender, slightly salty flavor with a subtle smoky aroma, ideal for sandwiches, salads, appetizers and hot dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Traditionally ham is prepared by dry‑curing and long‑term smoking, which gives it its characteristic scent.
Restaurants often use sliced ham as a quick protein source for “made‑to‑order” dishes.
There are several types of ham: boiled, smoked, dry‑cured (Parma) – each with distinct taste and texture.
Thin slices allow rapid, even heating in the oven or on a grill.
Ham is frequently served as a “roll‑up” – a roll of ham, cheese and herbs.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Ham provides about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Iron in ham helps maintain normal hemoglobin levels.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Ham supplies B1, B3 and B12 vitamins, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Low in carbohydrates
items.content: Suitable for low‑carb diets as it contains virtually no sugars.

items.title: Zinc content
items.content: Zinc supports immune function and wound healing.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Because ham is often salty, people with hypertension should limit intake.

items.title: Preservatives and nitrites
items.content: Some hams contain nitrites, which can be harmful in excess.

items.title: Pork allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience allergic reactions to pork.

items.title: Digestive discomfort
items.content: The high protein and salt levels may cause discomfort for those with gastrointestinal issues.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Ham can be enjoyed cold as a snack, added to sandwiches, salads, pasta, pizza, or quickly sautéed in a pan. Thin slices are perfect for rolls and canapés.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store ham in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0‑4 °C. After opening, it is best consumed within 5–7 days. When frozen, it can be kept for up to 2 months if vacuum‑packed.
